title: Vesper and the Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Ivo Whitlock is summoned to read the will of shipping magnate Edmund Vesper, only to find a document no court has ever seen and a beneficiary who died a decade ago. When a stranger washes up on the estate's tidal flats wearing Ivo's own stolen clothes, he becomes both suspect and investigator, forced to untangle a cipher-encrypted ledger that reveals Vesper's fortune was built on smuggling and betrayal. As the tide uncovers evidence implicating every heir, Ivo discovers the will was forged by Vesper's secret daughter, who killed to reclaim an inheritance denied her—and in the final confrontation at the waterline, Ivo must choose between exposing her and protecting the one person who ever saw him clearly.
about_author: Cyrus Brightwater spent fifteen years as a probate clerk in coastal New England before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange inheritances and quiet grudges he witnessed firsthand. He writes from a converted boathouse where, he insists, nothing suspicious has ever washed ashore.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't Filed
chapters.summary: Ivo Whitlock arrives at Vesper House to read a will that exists in no registry, drafted on paper older than its signatures. The heirs—a widow, two sons, a business partner—watch him with barely concealed hostility. In third-person limited POV from Ivo. Emotional beat: unease; Ivo's instinct for paperwork tells him something is profoundly wrong.

chapters.title: A Stranger in My Clothes
chapters.summary: Dawn brings police to the tidal flats: a drowned man wearing Ivo's suit, his wallet, his watch. Detective Maren Okaeda treats Ivo as suspect first, witness second. Ivo recognizes the dead man as the 'deceased' beneficiary named in the will—alive until yesterday. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: fear curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Ledger of Salt and Ink
chapters.summary: Searching Vesper's study, Ivo finds a shipping ledger whose columns are nonsense numbers—until he notices recurring figures matching dates in the will. A cipher, hidden in plain sight among legitimate accounts. Meanwhile Okaeda reveals the clothes were taken from Ivo's hotel room. Third-person limited, alternating with Okaeda's case notes. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt overtaking fear.

chapters.title: What the Heirs Buried
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews each heir. The elder son lies about being at sea; the business partner's alibi cracks under one question; the widow quotes the will verbatim though she claims never to have read it. Each knows more than they admit. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: mounting paranoia—everyone is performing grief.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Decoding the cipher's first layer, Ivo learns Vesper had a daughter, Elowen, officially lost at sea ten years ago—the same year the ledger's entries turn dark. Her death certificate bears Ivo's own firm's stamp, filed by his late mentor. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: vertigo; the mystery has been waiting inside his own history.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Okaeda confronts Ivo with evidence someone entered his room using a key signed out by Vesper's housekeeper—who vanished the night of the drowning. Ivo realizes the frame was prepared weeks ago, meaning the killer planned the body before the will reading. Third-person limited, Okaeda primary. Emotional beat: dread shifting toward reluctant alliance between suspect and detective.

chapters.title: Every Cipher Is a Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo cracks the full cipher: the ledger records payments to silence witnesses of a crewman's murder aboard Vesper's flagship—witnessed by young Elowen. Her 'drowning' was exile arranged by her father; her return was the inheritance the will secretly restores. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: pity replacing suspicion; the crime has a wound at its center.

chapters.title: The House Remembers
chapters.summary: Someone burns the study. Ivo saves the ledger from the flames and catches a figure fleeing—small, sure-footed, wearing boots he last saw on the drowned man. The heirs' alibis collapse simultaneously; all were at the shore that night. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into certainty that the killer is still circling.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: At low tide, the sea returns what it took: the housekeeper's body, and in her pocket, a second cipher key. Confronted, Elowen Vesper—alive, disguised as the estate archivist—confesses she killed only the blackmailer who threatened to expose her, then dressed him in Ivo's clothes to buy time. She begs Ivo to let the will stand. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: the climax of love against duty.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Ivo files everything: the true will, the decoded ledger, his testimony. Elowen surrenders without running, asking only that the crewman's name be read aloud in court. Okaeda closes the case; the estate passes to trust, its corruption documented. Ivo, no longer invisible, keeps the tide table marked for next year. Third-person limited, Ivo. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—justice served, mercy earned, loneliness ended.
